claims.text: DFT-informed spin-lattice models can guide compositional tuning in non-equiatomic high-entropy-alloy thin films.
Compositional tuning can controllably adjust magnetic exchange interactions in these alloys.
Adjustment of magnetic exchange interactions can shift the magnetic transition temperature.
DFT-guided compositional tuning can enhance the magnetocaloric response.
The initial non-equiatomic HEA thin films or nanoparticles possess inherent compositional disorder.
First-principles DFT calculations can be used to derive atomistic spin-lattice Hamiltonians for the material.
Composition or microstructure can be adjusted according to predictions from the calculated spin-lattice Hamiltonians.
Subtle compositional changes alter magnetic exchange pathways.
Subtle compositional changes alter local spin alignments.
The proposed computational method captures the complex, disordered magnetic interactions of the HEA.
The model can predict how specific compositional adjustments modulate exchange interactions.
Modulation of exchange interactions changes the magnetic transition temperature.
Optimizing entropy change during a magnetic transition enhances the magnetocaloric effect.
The tuned alloy will exhibit a measurable shift in magnetic transition temperature relative to the untuned baseline.
The direction of the transition-temperature shift may be either upward or downward depending on the compositional adjustment.
The tuned alloy will have an enhanced magnetocaloric response under an applied magnetic field relative to the baseline.
The proposed effects are specifically applicable to low-dimensional non-equiatomic HEAs.
The approach may not directly extend to equiatomic HEAs or bulk materials because different microstructural factors may dominate.
Real-material disorder and low-dimensional surface effects make the magnitudes of transition-temperature and magnetocaloric changes uncertain.
